summary.en: Doing the right thing when the law doesn't give a clear answer.
summary.bs: Raditi ispravnu stvar kad zakon ne daje jasan odgovor.

en.one: Business ethics is about doing what's right in business, not only what's legal or profitable.
en.explain: The law sets the minimum. Ethics asks more: are we honest with customers, fair to staff and suppliers, careful with the environment? Many scandals started with things that were legal but clearly wrong, and ended up destroying trust.
en.example: A supplier sends a bigger delivery than invoiced by mistake. Legally unclear, ethically simple: you tell them.
en.why: Trust is slow to build and quick to lose. Ethical companies keep customers, attract good staff and avoid scandals.
en.mixup: Ethics isn't only for big corporations. In a small town, everyone hears about it when a small business cheats.

bs.one: Business ethics (poslovna etika) znači raditi ono što je ispravno u poslu, a ne samo ono što je zakonito ili profitabilno.
bs.explain: Zakon postavlja minimum. Etika traži više: jesmo li iskreni s kupcima, pošteni prema radnicima i dobavljačima, pažljivi prema okolini? Mnogi skandali su počeli stvarima koje su bile zakonite, ali očito pogrešne, i završili uništenim povjerenjem.
bs.example: Dobavljač greškom pošalje veću isporuku nego što je fakturisano. Pravno nejasno, etički jednostavno: javiš im.
bs.why: Povjerenje se gradi sporo, a gubi brzo. Etične firme zadržavaju kupce, privlače dobre ljude i izbjegavaju skandale.
bs.mixup: Etika nije samo za velike korporacije. U malom gradu svi čuju kad mala firma vara.

concepts.youtubeQuery: conflict of interest at work explained

en.one: A conflict of interest is when your personal interest could get in the way of doing your job fairly.
en.explain: Examples: hiring a relative, buying from a company you or your partner own, or judging a tender where a friend is bidding. Having a conflict isn't wrong in itself; hiding it is. The usual rule is: declare it and step back from the decision.
en.example: A purchasing manager's brother runs a printing shop that bids for the company's work. She tells her boss and lets a colleague choose the supplier.
en.why: Declared conflicts keep decisions fair and protect people from suspicion.
en.mixup: It doesn't matter if you'd decide fairly anyway. What matters is that others can trust the process.

bs.one: Conflict of interest (sukob interesa) je kad tvoj lični interes može stati na put tome da pošteno radiš svoj posao.
bs.explain: Primjeri: zapošljavanje rođaka, kupovina od firme koju posjeduješ ti ili partner, ili ocjenjivanje tendera na kojem učestvuje prijatelj. Imati sukob interesa nije samo po sebi pogrešno; skrivati ga jeste. Uobičajeno pravilo: prijavi ga i povuci se iz odluke.
bs.example: Bratu nabavne menadžerice pripada štamparija koja se javlja na posao firme. Ona to kaže šefu i pusti kolegu da izabere dobavljača.
bs.why: Prijavljeni sukobi čuvaju poštenje odluka i štite ljude od sumnje.
bs.mixup: Nije bitno bi li ti ionako odlučio pošteno. Bitno je da drugi mogu vjerovati procesu.

en.one: A code of conduct is a written set of rules and values that tells everyone in a company how to behave.
en.explain: It usually covers honesty, gifts and bribes, conflicts of interest, respect and harassment, data and confidentiality, and how to report problems. A good code is short, uses real examples and is backed by leaders who follow it themselves.
en.example: A company's code says staff may accept gifts worth up to 50 KM and must register anything above that. Everyone knows the rule, so awkward situations are easy to handle.
en.why: It turns values into clear everyday rules and gives people something to point to when under pressure.
en.mixup: A code nobody reads or that leaders ignore is worse than none. It teaches people the rules don't matter.

bs.one: Code of conduct (kodeks ponašanja) je pisani skup pravila i vrijednosti koji svima u firmi kaže kako se ponašati.
bs.explain: Obično pokriva iskrenost, poklone i mito, sukob interesa, poštovanje i uznemiravanje, podatke i povjerljivost, te kako prijaviti probleme. Dobar kodeks je kratak, koristi stvarne primjere, a podržavaju ga lideri koji ga i sami poštuju.
bs.example: Kodeks firme kaže da radnici smiju primiti poklone do 50 KM, a sve preko toga moraju evidentirati. Svi znaju pravilo, pa se nezgodne situacije lako rješavaju.
bs.why: Pretvara vrijednosti u jasna svakodnevna pravila i daje ljudima nešto na šta se mogu pozvati pod pritiskom.
bs.mixup: Kodeks koji niko ne čita ili koji lideri ignorišu je gori nego nikakav. Uči ljude da pravila nisu bitna.

en.one: Whistleblowing is when someone reports wrongdoing inside an organisation, like fraud, safety risks or corruption.
en.explain: Good companies offer a safe, confidential (often anonymous) way to report, take reports seriously and protect the reporter. In the EU, companies with 50+ employees must have an internal reporting channel, and whistleblowers are protected from retaliation by law.
en.example: An accountant notices invoices from a supplier that doesn't seem to exist. She reports it through the company's confidential channel, and an investigation uncovers fraud.
en.why: Most fraud is uncovered by tips from insiders. Listening early is far cheaper than finding out from the press.
en.mixup: Punishing or isolating the person who reports is illegal in many countries and kills any culture of honesty.

bs.one: Whistleblowing (prijavljivanje nepravilnosti) je kad neko prijavi nezakonito ili pogrešno ponašanje unutar organizacije, npr. prevaru, sigurnosne rizike ili korupciju.
bs.explain: Dobre firme nude siguran, povjerljiv (često anoniman) način prijave, ozbiljno shvataju prijave i štite osobu koja prijavljuje. U EU firme s više od 50 radnika moraju imati interni kanal za prijave, a zviždači su zakonom zaštićeni od odmazde.
bs.example: Računovođa primijeti fakture dobavljača koji kao da ne postoji. Prijavi to kroz povjerljivi kanal firme i istraga otkrije prevaru.
bs.why: Većina prevara se otkrije zahvaljujući dojavama iznutra. Rano slušanje je mnogo jeftinije nego saznati iz medija.
bs.mixup: Kažnjavanje ili izolovanje osobe koja prijavi je u mnogim zemljama nezakonito i ubija svaku kulturu iskrenosti.

concepts.youtubeQuery: how to solve an ethical dilemma at work

en.one: An ethical dilemma is a situation where every option has a moral cost, and the right choice isn't obvious.
en.explain: Simple tests help: Is it legal? Would I be comfortable if it was on the front page? Is it fair to everyone affected? Would I accept it if I were on the other side? Talking it through with someone you trust also helps.
en.example: Business is slow and you could keep everyone employed by quietly cutting product quality. Or you could keep quality and lay off two people. Both options hurt someone.
en.why: Thinking it through in a structured way leads to decisions you can defend and live with.
en.mixup: A dilemma isn't the same as a temptation. If one option is clearly wrong but profitable, that's a temptation, not a dilemma.

bs.one: Ethical dilemma (etička dilema) je situacija u kojoj svaka opcija ima moralnu cijenu, a pravi izbor nije očigledan.
bs.explain: Pomažu jednostavni testovi: Je li zakonito? Bi li mi bilo prijatno da je to na naslovnoj strani? Je li pošteno prema svima koje pogađa? Bih li to prihvatio da sam na drugoj strani? Pomaže i razgovor s nekim kome vjeruješ.
bs.example: Posao ide sporo i mogao bi zadržati sve radnike tako što ćeš potajno smanjiti kvalitet proizvoda. Ili možeš zadržati kvalitet i otpustiti dvoje ljudi. Obje opcije nekoga povrijede.
bs.why: Strukturirano razmišljanje vodi do odluka koje možeš odbraniti i s kojima možeš živjeti.
bs.mixup: Dilema nije isto što i iskušenje. Ako je jedna opcija očito pogrešna, ali profitabilna, to je iskušenje, a ne dilema.

en.one: Shareholders own the company. Stakeholders are everyone affected by it: staff, customers, suppliers, the local community and the environment.
en.explain: One view says a company's main job is to make profit for its owners. Another says it must balance the interests of all stakeholders. In practice, ignoring stakeholders usually hurts profit in the long run.
en.example: A factory could save money by dumping waste in the river. Shareholders might gain short-term, but the town, the river and eventually the company's reputation would pay.
en.why: It helps you see who really depends on your decisions, and who can help or hurt your business.
en.mixup: Caring about stakeholders doesn't mean ignoring profit. A company that loses money can't help anyone for long.

bs.one: Shareholders (dioničari, vlasnici) posjeduju firmu. Stakeholders (interesne strane) su svi na koje firma utiče: radnici, kupci, dobavljači, lokalna zajednica i okolina.
bs.explain: Jedno gledište kaže da je glavni posao firme da zaradi profit za vlasnike. Drugo kaže da mora balansirati interese svih interesnih strana. U praksi, ignorisanje interesnih strana dugoročno obično šteti profitu.
bs.example: Fabrika bi mogla uštedjeti bacanjem otpada u rijeku. Vlasnici bi kratkoročno dobili, ali bi grad, rijeka i na kraju ugled firme platili.
bs.why: Pomaže ti da vidiš ko stvarno zavisi od tvojih odluka i ko može pomoći ili naštetiti tvom poslu.
bs.mixup: Briga o interesnim stranama ne znači ignorisati profit. Firma koja gubi novac ne može dugo nikome pomagati.

options.bs: Prijaviti to i povući se iz odluke

q.en: Which question is a classic quick ethics test?
q.bs: Koje pitanje je klasičan brzi etički test?

options.en: Would I be OK if this was on the front page?
options.bs: Bi li mi bilo u redu da je ovo na naslovnoj strani?

explain.en: If you'd be embarrassed to see it published, think again.
explain.bs: Ako bi te bilo sramota da to vidiš objavljeno, razmisli ponovo.

q.en: Which group are stakeholders but not shareholders?
q.bs: Koja grupa su interesne strane, ali ne i vlasnici?

explain.en: Stakeholders include everyone affected by the company, not only its owners.
explain.bs: Interesne strane su svi na koje firma utiče, ne samo vlasnici.
